**Astur v2.6.2** — the taskbar can hide behind your windows, and the main key
gained a move mode.

## Download

`astur-windows-x64.zip` — unzip it anywhere and run `astur.exe`. No installer, no
admin rights. The zip holds two files side by side:

- `astur.exe` — the window manager (single Rust binary)
- `astur_settings.py` — the settings editor (Python 3 with tkinter)

## What's new

### The taskbar can get out of the way

`hide_taskbar = true` makes the Windows taskbar invisible and click-through: the
mouse passes to the window underneath, and nothing peeks out when a window is
maximised. An Explorer restart is picked up on the next check, so a rebuilt
taskbar is hidden again by itself.

The hotkey (`main_key` + `K`, `hide_taskbar_hotkey` to change it) brings the
taskbar back for a moment: it slides out, Win+B puts the keyboard focus on the
tray as Windows normally does, and once it slides away on its own Astur hides it
again. Press the hotkey a second time to cancel and hide it at once.

The default is off; nothing changes unless you ask for it.

### Move windows without holding a key

Double-tap the main key (within 400 ms) to enter move mode: the arrow keys move
the focused window and `Shift`+arrows resize it, with no modifier held. The
first arrow key press leaves the mode, and so do `Esc` and a third tap on the
main key. A small hint appears on the status bar while the mode is on.

### Three more workspace keys, and the system menu moved

`key_switch_ws_4`, `_5` and `_6` (default `l`, `;` and `'`) join the first three:
on several monitors they go to workspace 1/2/3 of the next monitor; on a single
monitor they go to workspaces 4/5/6. With `Shift` they carry the focused window
along, as the other workspace keys do.

The power menu moved from `'` to `main_key` + `M` (`key_system_menu = M`), which
keeps `'` free for the sixth workspace key.

The navbar can now draw the window title in bold (`title_bold`).

## Fixed

- **The taskbar hotkey never reached Win+B**: the injected shortcut was skipped
  whenever a modifier was still down, and the hotkey itself is a modifier plus a
  key, so it never fired. It now waits for the keys to be released (up to two
  seconds), and releases any stragglers first.
- **Hold-time races with the reveal**: injecting Win+B while `Alt` was still
  down made Windows see **Win+Alt+B**, the HDR toggle, and the Xbox Game Bar
  announced "Display does not support HDR". Astur now waits for a quiet 60 ms
  after the last modifier is released before it injects anything.
- **Taskbar restore order**: switching `hide_taskbar` off, and quitting Astur,
  now remove the transparent style *before* stopping the worker, so the taskbar
  can never be left invisible with nobody watching it.
- **The hotkey test on `main` was red**: the old-lookup oracle did not know
  `key_switch_ws_4/5/6`. Fixed, so the test suite is green again.
- **Settings**: the editor window opens centred and comes to the front instead of
  behind a topmost window, and every widget's font follows the UI size.

## Settings editor

- Covers **121** `astur.conf` keys and **74** `navbar.conf` keys — checked one by
  one against the built-in templates, nothing missing and nothing extra.
- New **Taskbar hiding** page with both taskbar keys.
- The key dropdowns now list A–Z, 0–9, F1–F24 and the punctuation keys; before
  they only offered the special keys, so `D`, `K` or `A` could not be picked.
- Saving keeps comments, blank lines and the original line endings, writes a
  `.bak` next to the file, and Astur applies the result within about a tenth of
  a second.

## Notes

- Your existing `%USERPROFILE%\.astur\astur.conf` is never rewritten. The new
  keys reach new installs, and **Restore defaults** in the editor picks up the
  new defaults per section.
- `settings_python` still points Astur at a specific Python when the one on
  `PATH` is not the one you want.
